mostWorthwhile.text: Making the first star was most worthwhile: the image is striking, and the distinction between fusion and ordinary flame makes the mythic recipe more educationally honest.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making mist and then a dense cloud felt somewhat routine, especially with only one combination offered at each step, though it eventually clarified the path to a star.

surprise.text: Earth and dust producing gravity surprised me; its role in gathering worlds was clear, but the recipe itself was abstract.

arbitrary.text: Combining the first star with air to make a starfield felt arbitrary: air's contribution was unclear, even though the resulting path to a galaxy made sense.

continue.text: Yes. The galaxy provides a satisfying stopping point, but its question about what else a star can give makes me curious to see how the world develops.
